content: 1. Indicator: Existence of National and Subnational Standards for Social Accountability in Accreditation Mechanisms This indicator assesses whether national or subnational standards for social accountability are integrated into accreditation mechanisms. It evaluates the inclusion of social accountability in these standards and the involvement of civil society, social stakeholders, and communities in the accreditation process. The data is disaggregated by health workforce education and training programs and is reported every three years. Potential data sources include ministries of health, higher education, national accreditation authorities, and professional bodies. 2. Indicator: Implementation of Social Accountability Standards in Accreditation Mechanisms This indicator examines whether national or subnational accreditation mechanisms for health workforce education and training institutions require mandatory reporting on the implementation of social accountability standards. Data is reported every three years, with sources including ministries of health, higher education, and professional associations. 3. Indicator: Existence of Standards for Social Determinants of Health in Accreditation Mechanisms This indicator evaluates whether social determinants of health are reflected in national or subnational standards for accreditation. Data is reported every three years, with potential sources including ministries of health, higher education, and national accreditation authorities. 4. Indicator: Existence of Standards for Interprofessional Education in Accreditation Mechanisms This indicator determines whether interprofessional education is included in national or subnational accreditation standards. Data is reported every three years, with sources such as ministries of health, higher education, and professional bodies. 5. Indicator: Cooperation Between Health Workforce Education Institutions and Regulatory Bodies on Accreditation Standards This indicator assesses the existence of coordination mechanisms between health workforce education institutions and regulatory bodies to agree on accreditation standards. It evaluates stakeholder involvement and institutional mechanisms for coordinating accreditation systems. Data is reported every three years, with sources including ministries of health, higher education, and national accreditation authorities. 6. Indicator: It also evaluates the integration of CPD into national education plans for the health workforce. Data is reported every three years, with sources such as ministries of health, higher education, and professional associations. 7. Indicator: Existence of In-Service Training in National Education Plans for the Health Workforce This indicator evaluates whether in-service training is integrated into national education policies and plans, considering strategies for professional, technical, and vocational education, as well as adult learning. Data is reported annually, with sources including ministries of health, higher education, and labor. 8. Module: Financing of Health Workforce Education and Training This module addresses the financing and investment in health workforce education and training. It tracks expenditures on education and training, including tuition fees, costs per graduate, and investment in transformative education. Data is reported annually, with sources such as ministries of finance, health, and education. 9. Indicator: Data is reported annually, with sources including financial management systems and national education accounts. 10. Indicator: Average Tuition Fee per Student in Health Workforce Education This indicator calculates the average tuition fee per student enrolled in health workforce education programs, excluding those exempt from fees. Data is reported annually, with sources such as ministries of finance and education. 11. Indicator: Investment in Transformative Education and Training This indicator evaluates the existence of national strategies and financing reforms that allocate adequate resources for transformative education. It assesses mechanisms for sustainable financing and guidance on lifelong learning systems. Data is reported annually, with sources including ministries of finance, health, and education. 12. Indicator: Data is reported annually, with sources such as financial management systems and education institutions. 13. Indicator: Cost per Graduate of Medical Specialist Education Programs This indicator calculates the recurrent costs of medical specialist education per graduate, disaggregated by specialty and institutional sector. Data is reported annually, with sources including ministries of finance and education. 14. Indicator: Data is reported annually, with sources such as ministries of finance and education. 15. Indicator: Total Expenditure on In-Service Training and Continuing Professional Development This indicator evaluates total expenditure on in-service training and CPD, disaggregated by occupation and funding source. Data is reported annually, with sources including ministries of finance, health, and education. 16. Module: Health Labour Market Flows This module addresses entries into and exits from the health labor market, as well as labor market imbalances. It monitors domestic efforts, dependency on foreign health workers, and voluntary and involuntary exits. Indicators include graduate entry rates, replenishment rates, and unemployment and vacancy rates. 17. Indicator: It includes those starting internships or residency training. Data is reported annually, with sources such as health workforce registries and professional associations. 18. Indicator: Replenishment Rate from Domestic Efforts This indicator calculates the ratio of newly active domestically trained health workers to the total stock of active health workers. It includes those returning to practice after temporary leave. Data is reported annually, with sources such as health workforce registries and professional associations. 19. Indicator: Data is reported annually, with sources such as health workforce registries and professional associations.
